definitions.gloss: working adult, full member of society
definitions.explanation: A person who has entered the workforce and participates in society as a responsible adult. In Japan this marks a significant life stage, typically beginning after graduation when one starts full-time employment. Contrasts with {学生|がくせい} (student).

examples.japanese: {来年|らいねん}から{社会人|しゃかいじん}になる。
examples.english: I will become a working adult starting next year.

examples.japanese: {社会人|しゃかいじん}としてのマナーを{身|み}につける。
examples.english: To learn proper manners as a working adult.

examples.japanese: {社会人|しゃかいじん}になって{初|はじ}めて、{親|おや}のありがたさが{分|わ}かった。
examples.english: It was only after becoming a working adult that I understood how grateful I should be to my parents.

notes:
USAGE:
A culturally important Japanese concept with no exact English equivalent. {社会人|しゃかいじん} marks the transition from student life to the adult working world. It carries connotations of responsibility, independence, and social contribution that go beyond simply having a job.

The term is often used when discussing life milestones, career transitions, and the expectations placed on adults in Japanese society.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {社会人|しゃかいじん}になる: to become a working adult
- {社会人|しゃかいじん}として: as a member of society
- {社会人|しゃかいじん}{一年目|いちねんめ}: first year as a working adult
- {新|しん}{社会人|しゃかいじん}: newly working adult (fresh graduate entering workforce)
